- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to adjust — apply downward drag or lagged smoothing to prevent overreaction.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility penalty to forecast.
- When bullish sentiment is low but supply is negative, model often ignores policy/structural pressure — force a slight downward drift even if sentiment is neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes followed by recovery, model tends to over-predict recovery — apply mean reversion filter with 3-5 day decay.
- In multi-event windows (e.g., 3+ auctions in 7 days), model fails to account for cumulative supply shock — adjust forecast by adding cumulative supply net as a downward offset.
- If true outcome shows “rebound after crash” (e.g., 50-60% drop then 20-30% recovery), model often fails to capture the lag — delay recovery forecast by 2-3 days or apply exponential decay to momentum.
